Title: Diagnosis of test `testCompareTo_otherEnumType`

Details: The test `testCompareTo_otherEnumType` in `ValuedEnumTest` is designed to verify that the `compareTo` method of `ValuedEnum` throws a `ClassCastException` when an attempt is made to compare two enum instances of different types (`ValuedColorEnum.BLUE` and `ValuedLanguageEnum.ENGLISH`).

Looking at the implementation of `ValuedEnum.compareTo(Object other)`, the method casts the `other` object to `ValuedEnum` without any type check, then performs subtraction on their internal integer values (`iValue`). This cast will succeed because both `ValuedColorEnum` and `ValuedLanguageEnum` inherit from `ValuedEnum`.

However, since the subtraction operation is performed on the integer values, the comparison does not inherently check if `other` is from the same subclass. Therefore, no `ClassCastException` is thrown by the cast (it's legal as they share the same parent class). As a result, the code just returns the difference of the values, which means the exception expected by the test on line 109 does not occur, causing the test failure.

The root cause of the bug is that the `compareTo` method does not check that the `other` object is of the exact same enum subclass type before comparing values. This allows cross-class comparisons which the test expects to be disallowed via `ClassCastException`.

Fixing the bug would require modifying `ValuedEnum.compareTo` to check the class of `other` and throw `ClassCastException` if it is a different subclass, thereby ensuring type-safe comparisons as the test intends.

Methods best suited for the fix:
org.apache.commons.lang.enums.ValuedEnum.compareTo(java.lang.Object)
